question.text: A condenser of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>2</mn><mo> </mo><mi>μ</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">F</mi></math> capacitance is charged steadily from <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>0</mn></math> to <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>5</mn><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">C</mi></math>. Which of the following graph represents correctly the variation of potential difference<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mfenced><mi>V</mi></mfenced></math> across its plates with respect to the charge <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mfenced><mi>Q</mi></mfenced></math> on the condenser?

solution.text:
The charge on a condenser is given by Q=CV.

⇒V=1CQ

Since the capacitance depends on the construction of the condenser, it is constant. Therefore, the graph will be straight line with slope =1C.
Slope =1C=12×10-6=5×105
